## Summary
- Add a small built-in provider default set: Codex `gpt-5.5` and Claude `claude-opus-4-8`.
- Preserve route/workflow reasoning defaults on top of the Codex model default; #388 composes these into effective ACP ids such as `gpt-5.5/medium`, `gpt-5.5/high`, or `gpt-5.5/xhigh` before acpx sees them.
- Preserve `AGENT_MODEL_POLICY` override precedence on top of built-in defaults.
- Route fixed Claude/Codex review lanes through `resolve-agent-provider` so they receive pinned/provider-specific model settings.
- Update docs for built-in defaults, reviewer lane behavior, and Claude Code minimum guidance for Opus 4.8.

## Tests
- `cd .agent && npm run build && node --test dist/__tests__/resolve-agent-provider.test.js dist/__tests__/envelope.test.js dist/__tests__/docs-validation.test.js dist/__tests__/acpx-adapter.test.js`

Stacked on #388. Supersedes the default-pinning portions of #380 with Codex model naming fixed first.

Closes #375.

## Summary of PR/Issue

PR #389 adds a frozen `BUILTIN_PROVIDER_DEFAULTS` map (`codex → gpt-5.5`, `claude → claude-opus-4-8`) as the lowest-precedence layer in `resolveRunConfig`, so reviewer lanes now have a sensible model without requiring an explicit `AGENT_MODEL_POLICY`. Each reviewer lane in `agent-review.yml` is routed through `resolve-agent-provider` before runtime setup, pinning the provider via `route_provider: ${{ matrix.agent }}` while still allowing policy overrides to take effect. The PR is stacked on #388 (Codex ACP normalization), which is required for the `gpt-5.5` built-in to be composed correctly into ACP model ids. Documentation is updated across four files.

## Review

The implementation is correct, minimal, and the existing resolver is reused without adding a separate registry. Both warnings are known operational conditions — not code defects — that are already documented in the PR.

| Issue | Severity | Description |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Merge dependency on #388 | WARNING | #389 must not merge before #388; without acpx normalization, `gpt-5.5` is passed to acpx un-composed and the Codex reviewer lane will fail. |
| `claude-opus-4-8` requires Claude Code ≥ v2.1.154 on self-hosted runners | WARNING | Older self-hosted runner installs will fail on the Claude reviewer lane; if both lanes fail, synthesis fails hard. `claude update` is the mitigation and is documented. |
| Imprecise regex in `envelope.test.ts` | INFO | `assert.match(reviewWorkflow, /route:\s*review/)` also matches `route: review-synthesize`; passes now but could mask a future step id swap. The `id: reviewer_provider` assertion provides sufficient protection. |
| Empty-string route override now has new semantics | INFO | The unchanged `null/empty` test in `resolve-agent-provider.test.ts` passes, but `model: ""` now acts as an explicit escape hatch that clears the built-in default rather than being a no-op. |
| `required:` input omitted from reviewer lane resolver step | INFO | Since `route_provider` is always `codex` or `claude` from the matrix, the required-check path never triggers; behavior is correct but the omission is worth noting. |
| No actionable code defects | INFO | All five findings above are INFO/WARNING-level operational or minor test clarity items. No BLOCKING issues found. |

## Progress

- Rubrics review posted to PR as comment `IC_kwDOSOhEMM8AAAABEYMsaw`: **100/100 PASS** across 9 rubrics (surgical changes, reuse, minimal defaults, docs sync, structured inputs, documentation quality).
- `AGENT_MODEL_POLICY` precedence is preserved: built-in is explicitly the lowest layer, policy default → provider overrides → route overrides all win.
- `action.yml` `model` output description corrected ("if configured" removed) — accurate since model is now always emitted.
- `doesNotMatch` removal in `envelope.test.ts` is intentional: the reviewer step now always emits a model, so the old assertion that no model appeared was stale.
- Rubrics reviewer (Codex lane) failed with 401 (fake API key in test environment); rubrics review was completed separately and already posted to the PR.
- No existing inline review threads or inline comments on this PR; no inline comment actions taken.

## Issue Details

<details>
<summary>Merge dependency on #388</summary>

**Cause:** `gpt-5.5` is the built-in Codex default and is passed as `model` to `run-agent-task` → acpx. PR #388 adds the normalization that converts `{ model: "gpt-5.5", reasoning_effort: "xhigh" }` into the ACP model id `gpt-5.5/xhigh`. Without #388, acpx receives a bare model name where it expects a composed ACP id.

**Candidate solutions:** Merge #388 first (the PR is already open and stacked). No code change in #389 is needed; this is a sequencing constraint.

**Comments:** The PR body already states "Stacked on #388." This is the primary merge-readiness gate.

</details>

<details>
<summary>`claude-opus-4-8` requires Claude Code ≥ v2.1.154 on self-hosted runners</summary>

**Cause:** Older CLI builds do not know the `claude-opus-4-8` model id. GitHub-hosted runners are unaffected (fresh install each run). Self-hosted runners with a cached CLI older than v2.1.154 will fail at agent startup for the Claude reviewer lane.

**Candidate solutions:** Run `claude update` on all self-hosted runner hosts (documented in `self-hosted-github-action-runner.md`). No code change needed. A pre-flight version check in `setup-agent-runtime` would be a hardening option but is out of scope for this PR.

**Comments:** The Claude reviewer job is `continue-on-error: true`, so a single-lane failure degrades gracefully if the Codex lane succeeds. Dual-lane failure would cause synthesis to fail; that scenario requires both the Claude CLI version gap and a Codex credential issue simultaneously.

</details>

## Recommended Next Step

**HUMAN_DECISION** — both warnings are documented operational sequencing constraints (merge ordering and runner version), not code defects; no automated fix-pr pass can resolve them. A maintainer should confirm #388 is merged before landing this PR.

## Final Verdict

**MINOR_ISSUES**

## Action Items

- [ ] Merge PR #388 before merging PR #389 to ensure `gpt-5.5` is correctly composed into ACP model ids by acpx normalization.
- [ ] Verify self-hosted runner hosts have Claude Code ≥ v2.1.154 installed (run `claude update` if needed) before the Claude reviewer lane goes live.

ok but the question is that, we already want to have two separate models (codex and claude when available) as for a matrix to run it; i am not sure if this change meaningfully fix this issue?

You’re right to separate those concerns.

This change does **not** meaningfully fix “run two separate reviewer lanes, Codex and Claude when available.” That behavior already existed in the matrix: one `codex` lane and one `claude` lane.

What this change fixes is narrower: the reviewer lanes now use the same provider resolver path so they receive the pinned/provider-specific model config. Without this, the matrix still runs two lanes, but the lanes do not get the new built-in defaults from this PR (`gpt-5.5` / `claude-opus-4-8`) or provider-level `AGENT_MODEL_POLICY` model overrides.

So the honest framing is:

- If the issue is **“review should run both Codex and Claude lanes”**, this workflow change is not the fix.
- If the issue is **“review lanes should use Sepo’s pinned model defaults / provider-specific model policy instead of whatever the provider runtime defaults to”**, then this change is needed.
- It also does **not** add “when available” gating; the workflow still attempts both lanes and relies on `continue-on-error` if one provider is unavailable.

If we want the PR to stay focused only on provider default pinning, I’d describe this as “applying pinned model defaults to the existing review matrix lanes,” not as fixing the existence of the two-lane review matrix.

@sepo-agent /answer why https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/pull/389 is not merged when we merge #390? (I think they are all stacked?

Because #390 was merged into `main`, but #389’s PR base is still `agent/codex-acp-model-normalization` (#388’s branch), not `main`.

Current stack state I found:

- #388: `agent/codex-acp-model-normalization` → `main`, merged.
- #389: `agent/pin-effective-model-defaults` → `agent/codex-acp-model-normalization`, still open.
- #390: `agent/default-visible-model-display` → `main`, merged.

#390’s merged commit list included the stack commits from #388 and #389:

- `165eeae` - #388
- `bd216e2` - #389
- `02c87cc` - #390

So the **code from #389 did land through #390**, but GitHub did not mark PR #389 itself as merged because the PR record for #389 was not merged into its configured base branch. GitHub does not reliably cascade-close stacked PRs just because a later PR carried the same commits into `main`.

At this point #389 is effectively already included via #390. The clean follow-up is either:

- retarget #389 to `main`; it should become empty/already included, then close it, or
- close #389 manually as superseded/already landed via #390.

The confusing part is that #390 said “Stacked on #389” but was opened against `main`, so merging it merged the whole stack into `main` instead of advancing/merging the intermediate #389 PR record.
